title: Delegated rollout tokens and per-route idempotent client primitives for safe canary & shadow
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Teams using the rollout APIs often need a narrow-scoped token and client-side primitives to safely orchestrate canary/A-B/shadow exposures without granting full rollout control to downstream services. Current rollout helpers require service credentials that are too permissive and lack idempotent primitives for retry-safe client SDKs. This causes operational risk (accidental overexposure), audit gaps, and complex per-team firewalling.

Goal: Implement a delegated rollout token surface and a small set of idempotent client primitives (exposure reservation, commit, reconcile, and shadow-mirror call IDs) to enable:
- Per-route least-privilege tokens that can be minted by the control plane for short-lived clients (edge proxies, mobile gateways, experiment platforms).
- Idempotent operations so clients can safely retry without risking duplicate exposures or double-counted traffic for billing and guardrail logic.
- Clear audit and trace linkage from client-side exposure to rollout control plane (token metadata, request IDs, signed receipts).
- Fast auto-rollback hooks when experiment health signals exceed thresholds.

Scope: API surface, SDK helpers (Go, TypeScript), server-side admission checks, token minting flow, audit metadata, and e2e test harness for canary+shadow scenarios. Not in scope: UX console changes (will be a follow-up PM ticket) and long-term token rotation automation (separate infra project).
acceptance_criteria: AuthZ: Control plane can issue delegated rollout tokens scoped to a route/id and time-limited (TTL).
APIs: New endpoints for reserveExposure(commitableId), commitExposure(commitableId, token), reconcileExposure(commitableId) exposed in public SDKs (TS/Go).
Idempotency: commitExposure is idempotent across retries and returns stable exposure IDs; duplicate commits must not increase traffic counters or change traffic split state.
Audit: Every delegated token mint and exposure commit is logged with token issuer, client service, route, and commitableId; logs are queryable for 90 days.
Auto-rollback: runtime hooks detect experiment health breaches and can programmatically reduce exposure to 0 for tokens issued in a time window (integration test verifies rollback).
Docs: API reference, quickstart for edge gateway integration, and a migration guide for teams using broad rollout credentials.
SDKs: TypeScript and Go SDKs provide clear helper functions and release notes; unit tests cover retry paths and concurrency edge cases.
tasks: Design token format and claims (route, issuer, ttl, nonce) - API design doc created
Implement token mint endpoint in control plane with scoped RBAC enforcement
Add server-side admission check to validate token on exposure endpoints
Ship TS and Go SDK helpers with idempotency key handling and local retry backoff
Add integration tests: canary flow, shadow mirror flow, concurrent commits, and rollback scenario
Add audit events to event store and dashboard wiring (90d retention)
Prepare migration doc and runbook for on-call when rollouts use delegated tokens
